properties.name: A refused write stores nothing: one write unit per served tool call, settled at call_tool; batches nest; reads in a batch see its writes
properties.rationale:
THE CAUSE (fact:root-cause-a-typed-constructor-writes-the-node-before-its-later-checks-and-a-refusal-leaves-it-2026-10-02, VS Code --call field report limitation 17): atomicity was a property of the bulk door only. Each typed handler was a sequence of individually durable upserts, and the rollback was hand-written per refusal (two of them, both guarded by !existed, so a revise kept its overwrite). Confirmed on main before the fix: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_refused_write_stores_nothing.rs failed there in 7 of 8 cases. Its walk named 6 refused calls that left a node: two of them constructors outside the triage's measured 13 (add_design_rule on `steps`, and snapshot_before_change, which left a ChangeEvent) and one a field the triage had not tried on a constructor it had (add_requirement on `provenance`).

THE CLASS, NOT THE 13: the unit sits at the one point every served write passes (call_tool), keyed on the catalogue's own read_only_hint, so a write tool added later joins by being served. The walk generates arguments for EVERY served write tool from its schema and asserts each refusal left the store identical.

WHAT A CALL-SIZED BATCH NEEDED THAT A BULK-SIZED ONE NEVER DID:
(1) nesting. A begin_batch inside a batch used to COMMIT the outer one, so an import or bulk form inside a call would have made the call's earlier writes durable.
(2) derived scans keyed on the write generation answered from before a batch's own writes (fact:a-derived-scan-inside-a-batch-answered-from-before-the-batchs-own-writes-2026-10-02).
(3) search. The duplicate guard looks for the node its own call just wrote, and Tantivy hides uncommitted text, so a search inside a batch now publishes the batch's text, and a discard re-derives every touched document from the store. Checked on a real RocksDB store with this branch's debug binary: a near-duplicate add_capability was refused naming its near-match, the node was absent afterwards, and search_design reported no stale hit. Recording this very change met it too: a link_artifact refused on artifact_type left no Artifact behind.

FOUND ON THE WAY, BY THE COMPILE GUARD (code read, not measured): review_relations took the raw graph lock rather than write_lock, so its writes skipped crediting, the agent stamp, signing, the write-generation bump and the write-through doorbell. It now goes through write_lock. A tool marked read-only that asks to write inside a served call is refused, so the annotation that decides who gets a unit cannot lie.

NOT COVERED, deliberately: files beside the store (identity label, usage ledger, handshake record, an export written to a path). The two hand-written rollbacks in tools/capture.rs are kept; the unit makes them redundant on the served path, and they still serve a handler called directly.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Every served write tool's call is one atomic unit of the store (DesignGraph::begin_unit/commit_unit/discard_unit over the existing batch). ReflowService::call_tool opens a CallUnit for a tool marked as a write, the handler's first write_lock takes the graph's write lock and opens the batch, and the unit is committed when the handler succeeds and discarded when it refuses. Batches nest as savepoints, so bulk forms, import and HEAL inside a call join its unit. Staged writes and discards move the write generation, and a search inside a batch publishes its text. SharedGraph leaves write_lock as the only door to &mut DesignGraph. A refused call no longer rings the write-through export.
